shared_elements: low-relief carved figural motifs on a stone surface
curvilinear/spiral forms (weathered spirals in A, ram horns in B)
justification: The only real correspondence is that both surfaces bear low-relief figural carving with rounded, curvilinear elements — eroded spiral/face-like motifs in A and the volute horns and eyes of the rams in B — which is a very generic resemblance. B depicts a legible naturalistic procession scene of two profile human figures leading two horned rams with modelled fleece and a winged form behind, whereas A shows only isolated schematic, boldly pecked curvilinear motifs with no discernible narrative or figure-to-figure relationship.
